elements.name: A1_T1
elements.html: Please spend a few minutes exploring the tool before beginning the survey. Click the icon in your browser toolbar near the top-right corner of the browser window. Be sure to view all parts of the interface.

elements.name: A1_Q1
elements.title: Briefly describe (1-2 sentences), what do you think is the purpose of this tool?

elements.name: A1_Q2
elements.title: Please list the new information, if any, you learned by using this tool.

elements.name: A1_Q3
elements.title: Please list the information you already knew, if any, that the tool told you.

elements.name: A1_Q4
elements.title: Please list the surprising information, if any, that the tool told you.

elements.name: A1_Q5
elements.title: What questions, if any, do you have about what you saw in the tool?

elements.name: A2_T1
elements.html: Next we would like to understand your thoughts, awareness, and comfort around Google Activity data after using our designed personalised dashboard (ADA) for a week.

elements.name: A2_Q1
elements.title: Compared to before your weeklong usage of ADA, how would you describe your overall awareness of what Google stores about your activity?

elements.name: A2_T2
elements.html:
Please rate your agreement with each statement below, grouped into three areas:

System Quality
Ease of Use & Interaction Experience
Perceived Usefulness

On a scale of 1 to 5, where 1 indicates “Strongly disagree” and 5 indicates “Strongly agree.”

elements.name: A2_Q2
elements.title: System Quality (Data, Recommendations & Clarity)

rows.text: The activity information shown in ADA regarding my activities felt accurate.
The activity information shown in ADA regarding my activities felt reliable.
The activity information provided by the extension matches my idea of how sensitive my browser interactions are.
I understand why ADA marked certain entries as more sensitive than the others.

elements.name: A2_Q3
elements.title: Ease of Use & Interaction Experience

rows.text: The extension is easy to navigate.
The extension is easy to interact with.
The activity information provided by the extension is easy for me to understand.
The order in which the recommendations are presented by the browser is easy for me to understand.
The extension was overall presented in a way that was easy for me to understand.

elements.name: A2_Q4
elements.title: Perceived Usefulness

rows.text: ADA helped me understand the potential 'sensitivity' of my data quickly.
ADA helped me notice things about my Google activity that I was not aware of before.
Using this extension would help me better manage my browsing data.
Using this extension would improve to remove sensitive data from being shipped to google.
I would be open to using this extension in my day-to-day life.
I trust the personalized dashboard provided by the system.
The personalized dashboard helps me decide which activities to delete.

elements.name: A2_Q5
elements.title: Privacy & Trust

rows.text: I trust that ADA handled all my data privately on my device.
Knowing my data never left my device made me feel safe using ADA.

elements.name: AC_2
elements.title: Please select "Disagree" for this statement so that we know you are reading carefully.

elements.name: A2_Q6
elements.title: How did you feel using ADA by the end of the 7-day period?

elements.name: A2_T3
elements.html:
Over the past week, ADA ranked and re-ordered your activity items. Thinking about how the tool ordered your activity items — please rate your agreement with each statement below, grouped into three areas:

Agreement
Stability
Trust and responsiveness

Answer choices for all questions in this section: Strongly agree · Agree · Neither agree nor disagree · Disagree · Strongly disagree

elements.name: A2_Q7
elements.title: Agreement

rows.text: The items the tool put at the top were the ones I also consider most sensitive.
The tool's ordering of the activity items reflected what matters to me personally.
The tool's ordering of the activity items seemed like it would be the same for anyone.

elements.name: A2_Q8
elements.title: Stability

rows.text: The tool's ordering of the activity items stayed consistent over the week.
When the ordering of the activity items changed, the changes made sense to me.
The ordering of the activity items changed more often than I would have liked.

elements.name: A2_Q9
elements.title: Trust and responsiveness

rows.text: The tool seemed to adjust to me (became more personalised) over the course of the week.
I could predict how the tool would treat a new item of my activity.

elements.name: A2_Q10
elements.title: Did you notice the tool's ordering change at any point during the week?

elements.name: A2_Q10_B1
elements.title: In your own words, what changed, and what did you make of it?

elements.name: A3_T1
elements.html: Over the past 7 days, ADA analysed your activity data locally on your browser and showed you the same in a personalised dashboard. No data ever left your device. Now, we will ask a few questions to understand your privacy preferences and comfort with this kind of sensitivity estimation.

elements.name: A3_Q1
elements.title: In the future, how would you prefer tools like ADA to handle your activity data? (Choose the option closest to your preference)
choices: Store all activity data and other attributes (e.g. sensitivity feedback) locally on my device indefinitely, until I choose to delete them
Store all activity data locally, but auto-delete items older than 3 months
Store all activity data locally, but auto-delete items older than 18 months
Do not store any activity data after sensitivity is shown — delete immediately after analysis
I would prefer an option where the model learns but keeps no history of my data

elements.name: A3_Q2
elements.title: Would you prefer to have an auto-delete option that deletes your sensitive data from the Google Activity dashboard?

elements.name: A3_Q3
elements.title: Based on your experience, how comfortable are you with ADA storing your sensitivity feedback locally on your device?

elements.name: A3_Q4
elements.title: Can you please briefly (1-3 sentences) explain your answer choice for the previous question?

elements.name: A3_T2
elements.html:
Rating Your Own Activity Items (again)

At the start of the study, we asked you to rate how sensitive you personally found nine items from your ADA list. We would like to ask the same thing once more, now that you have used ADA for a week. As before, you will not be asked to type or describe any of your activities.

elements.name: A3_T3
elements.html:
Step 1. Open the ADA dashboard. Your personalised activity dashboard presents all the recorded activity items.

Step 2. Find the following nine items from your personalised dashboard and keep them in mind. You may want to keep ADA open in a separate window while you answer.

Top 3
The 1st, 2nd, and 3rd items at the top of your list
Random 3
Three items picked at random from the rest of your list
Bottom 3
The last three items at the bottom of your list

Step 3. For each of these nine items, please tell us how sensitive you personally consider that activity to be.

elements.name: A3_Q5
elements.title: How sensitive do you personally consider each of these activity items to be?
elements.description: Here 1 means “Not sensitive at all” and 5 means “Very sensitive.”

rows.text: Item at position 1 (top of list)
Item at position 2
Item at position 3
First of the three middle items
Second of the three middle items
Third of the three middle items
Third-from-last item
Second-from-last item
Last item (bottom of list)

elements.name: A5_Q1
elements.title: Compared to before you used the tool, how likely are you to do each of the following now?

rows.text: Seek out more information about how companies store your activity
Review your Google activity history
Delete items from your activity history
Turn off or pause an Activity Control
Set your activity to auto-delete after a fixed period
Use Incognito mode or browse signed out

elements.name: A6_T1
elements.html: This section helps us understand your broader attitudes towards privacy. Your responses will help us interpret why different users engaged with ADA differently.

elements.name: A6_Q1
elements.title: For each pair below, imagine you had to choose between Option A and Option B. Please indicate which you would choose.

rows.text: A: Free access to services, but your activity is stored indefinitely. B: A monthly fee, but no activity is stored.
A: Your activity is deleted automatically after three months, but recommendations get worse. B: Your activity is kept forever, and recommendations stay accurate.
A: Your search results are not personalized, but nothing you search is stored. B: Your results are personalized, but everything you search is stored.
A: A company decides which of your activity is sensitive. B: You label which of your activity is sensitive yourself, but must do it manually.

elements.name: A6_T3
elements.html:
Now, we would like to understand your general preferences when it comes to balancing privacy, personalization, and convenience. Different people value these aspects differently, and there are no right or wrong responses.

Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with the following statements, on a scale of 1 to 5, where 1 indicates “Strongly disagree” and 5 indicates “Strongly agree.”

elements.name: A6_Q2
elements.title: Please rate your agreement with each statement.

rows.text: I prefer a personalized system that adapts using user feedback, even if it requires processing more data locally on the device.
I prefer less personalization if it guarantees that none of my data leaves my device.
I am willing to trade some convenience in exchange for stronger privacy protection.
I would prefer using ADA's dashboard over Google's default My Activity dashboard to review and manage my online activity.
If a tool gives me clear insights about sensitive data, I am more likely to use it regularly, even if it requires some effort from my side.

pages.name: A7
pages.title: Opinions about Activity Collection and Personalization

elements.name: A3_T1
elements.html: The following section repeats some of the questions you answered in the pre-usage part of this study. This is intentional: we would like to understand whether, and how, your opinions may have changed after using ADA for the past week. As before, during the rest of this survey, we use the term 'activity data' to refer to the records a company (e.g., Google) keeps of what you searched for, watched, visited, or did while using its services.

elements.name: A7_Q1
elements.title: Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with each of the following statements.

rows.text: I would like the services I use to be personalized based on my past activity, as opposed to being the same for everyone.
I would be comfortable with a company keeping a record of what I search for and watch.
If it were available, I would like to use a system that shows me what activity data has been collected about me.
I feel that companies adequately explain what they keep in my activity history.
I feel that I understand how companies decide what to keep in my activity history.
I would consider it fair for a company to store my activity in order to personalize the services I use.
I would consider it creepy for a company to store my activity in order to personalize the services I use.

elements.name: A*_Q1
elements.title: What pieces of activity data do you think Google collects when you use your Google Account on multiple devices? (Select all that apply)
choices: Approximate location at the time of activity
Interactions with ads (e.g., ads viewed or clicked)
Data shared with third-party apps using Google login
elements.noneText: I don’t think Google collects data across services

elements.name: A8_Q2
elements.title: Imagine a regular Google user with a normal account, using Google services with the default settings. How likely or unlikely do you expect it is that Google retains a record of the following?

rows.text: The text of every search they have typed
Searches they typed but did not submit
Which YouTube videos they watched, and for how long
Voice recordings from Assistant queries
Places they physically travelled to
Their contact list
The colour of the device they used
Which apps they opened on an Android phone
Ads they clicked
Searches made while signed out
Searches made in Incognito mode
The content of their emails
Their Social Security / national ID number
How many devices they use
Purchases confirmed by email

elements.name: A8_Q3
elements.title: In the last week, about how many searches do you think you made on Google?

elements.name: A8_Q4
elements.title: In the last week, about how many YouTube videos do you think you watched?

elements.name: A8_Q5
elements.title: In the last week, about how many separate items do you think were added to your Google activity dashboard?

elements.name: A8_Q6
elements.title: Of the items in your Google activity history, about what percentage do you think are still stored from more than a year ago?
elements.description: 0% = none of them; 100% = all of them.

elements.name: A8_Q7
elements.title: Which of the following privacy approaches would you prefer for managing your Google activity data (e.g., searches, browsing history, app activity, YouTube history) in the future?
choices: Give consent to Google to collect and store all activity data indefinitely, until I choose to delete it
Give consent to Google to collect and store all activity data, but require Google to delete any data older than 3 months
Give consent to Google to collect and store all activity data, but require Google to delete any data older than 18 months
Store all activity data only on my device, allow required computations to run on-device, and share only aggregated results with Google instead of full data
Do not give consent to Google to collect or store any of my activity data, and delete any data currently stored by Google immediately

elements.name: A8_Q8
elements.title: Do you believe that Google ensures the security of the activity data it stores?

elements.name: A8_Q9
elements.title: On a scale of 1 to 5, with 1 being the least and 5 being the most, how much do you trust Google not to misuse your activity data?

elements.name: A8_Q10
elements.title: Do you think that you can access your activity data collected by Google?

elements.name: A9_T1
elements.html: You have now been using the ADA extension, referred to as the “system” below, for the past week. This section presents a set of general statements about your overall experience interacting with it. Drawing on your usage over this period, please select the answer choice that best describes your agreement or disagreement with each statement.

elements.name: A9_Q1
elements.title: Please rate your agreement with each statement.

rows.text: I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
I found the system unnecessarily complex.
I thought the system was easy to use.
I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system.
I found the various functions in this system were well-integrated.
I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system.
I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
I found the system very cumbersome to use.
I felt very confident using the system.
I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system.

elements.name: A10_T1
elements.html: This section moves away from Google specifically and asks about your general views on how companies handle personal information online. There are no right or wrong answers — just tell us how much you agree or disagree with each statement below.

elements.name: A10_Q1
elements.title: Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with each of the following statements.

rows.text: Companies seeking information online should disclose the way the data are collected, processed, and used.
A good consumer online privacy policy should have a clear and conspicuous disclosure.
It is very important to me that I am aware and knowledgeable about how my personal information will be used.
It usually bothers me when online companies ask me for personal information.
When online companies ask me for personal information, I sometimes think twice before providing it.
It bothers me to give personal information to so many online companies.
I’m concerned that online companies are collecting too much personal information about me.
